full_judgment:
5. Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, does not dispute the decree for dissolution of marriage and the rate of maintenance allowed by the learned trial Court and affirmed by the learned Subordinate Judge. He simply disputes the order whereby both the courts below granted past maintenance to the opposite party and her child. In support of his contention he has placed reliance on section 278 of Mulla's Principles of Mohamedan Law (Eighteenth Edition) and two decisions reported in ILR 1881 (Cal) 631, and PLD (Lahore) 1958, 596. 

 6. Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, the learned advocate representing the opposite party has, on the other hand, argued that since the term "maintenance" has not been defined and has been left open in the Family Courts Ordinance 1985, it must be deemed,. to include past maintenance as well. He has also placed reliance on a decision reported in 1LR 1958 TC 690. 

 9. So far as the question of past maintenance for the child is concerned, there is no specific provision in the substantive law and Mr. Saha has relied on the decision in the case of Mst. Chulam Fatima, plaintiff appellant Vs. Sheikh Muhammad Bashir, Defendant-respondent, reported in PLD, 1958 (WP) (Lahore), 596. In this case, the wife claimed past maintenance from the father for her child by him and it was held that neither the child nor the person who maintains it can claim past maintenance from the father unless the same has been previously fixed either by a decree of the Court or by the father himself. Quoting from the Hedaya the learned Single Judge deciding the said case observed as follows: 

 "With regard to past maintenance decreed in respect of the child the appeal is clearly groundless. The father of the child the 1st defendant was bound to maintain it, and he is, therefore bound to pay the mother the expenses of the maintenance she incurred while it was staying with her." The learned Judge making the aforesaid observation has not, however, cited any authority for the aforesaid view taken by him and in view of the decision reported in PLD, 1958 (Lahore) 596 and the authorities referred to in that decision we are unable to accept the proposition regarding past maintenance to a child enunciated in AIR 1954 TC 432 relied upon by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah.
